body:
`.github/workflows/auto-merge.yml` sizes a tier-2 PR from
`gh pr view --json additions,changedFiles`, which is the raw diff. The
documented policy says the opposite:

    Test files (anything under `tests/`) don't count toward the cap —
    tests pin behavior, they don't introduce risk, and penalizing
    test-coverage would undermine the test-driven discipline below.
        — ~/.claude/skills/CWNG-tick/SKILL.md, "Autonomous test-driven
          merge + release"

So the gate penalises exactly the behaviour the project mandates
everywhere else. Observed on #1457: two changed production lines in
`cps/__init__.py`, plus a regression-test file and a changelog entry.

    auto-merge skipped: PR is too large for safe-tier-2
    (additions=149, files=3; caps are 80 LOC / 3 files)

The production diff was ~15 lines. The same fix shipped with no tests
would have auto-merged.

Nothing is unsafe here — demotion routes to `needs-review`, which is
autonomous — but it costs a review cycle on every well-tested small fix,
and it quietly teaches the wrong lesson: the cheapest way to keep a fix
in the fast lane is to not write the test.

Fix is to subtract test-path additions and files before the comparison,
in `auto-merge.yml`, sourcing the exclusion regex from
`.github/policy/tier-policy.config` so it stays the single source of
truth. `tests/autopilot/test_tier_policy.sh` should pin it: a PR of N
production lines plus a large test file must classify the same as one of
N production lines alone.

Found while shipping #1443.
title: Tier-2 auto-merge cap counts test files, so writing regression tests demotes your own PR
